notes.summary: Independent proofs of 300: explicit-global-Lipschitz exact cell extensions with whole affine-face traces, actual-face support preservation, proper rational-spatial REAL-PA affine auxiliaries, and legal −1/4 incompatible-gluing diagnostic. Separate full-affine majorants are also rederived; no global original-complex gluing theorem follows.
notes.detailedSummary: A rational split V=H⊕S and an independently proved face-distance bound ||t−z||≤K||s|| give F=inf_sigma(f+N), N=M||t||+B||s||, with M,B>L and B≥L(K+1)+MK. F is finite convex globally Lipschitz, exact on all sigma, with entire-H trace inf_tau(f_tau+Mnorm). Uniformly bounded supplied common p_y are preserved only at actual tau. The same infimum for an actual REAL affine ell positive on every nonzero original recession direction gives a proper full-page auxiliary and bounded F−Gamma. Finite lifted primal generators prove rational spatial geometry despite real heights. On three dependent pages, ell=s, M=2,B=4 gives F=−2t−s on s≥0,t+s≤0 and a legal rational PCC of cost −1/4 outside tau. Full-affine sample majorants have exact recession and finite rational contacts before decreasing shifts. These results require explicit GLOBAL cell Lipschitz hypotheses and do not import working299 or general PA density.
notes.text:
This is an unreviewed independent reconstruction, not a grant. The proofs below verify working300's seven units and its separate-affine approximation connection while retaining its outside-face gap. Ordinary real completeness, finite-dimensional compactness, rational linear algebra, and elementary convexity are disclosed foundations. No MA is used.

Finite polyhedral tools. A nonnegative representation in a finite real cone reduces to an independent active subset: for a dependence b, change its sign so some b_j>0 and replace coefficients a by a−tb, t=min_{b_j>0}a_j/b_j. This keeps coefficients nonnegative and eliminates one. The inverse of each independent column map bounds coefficients by C_I times the represented norm. A converging sequence has a subsequence using one of finitely many subsets and convergent bounded coefficients; therefore the cone is closed, also with both signs of a lineality basis. For an inequality cone, quotient its kernel using a rational complement for rational data. The sum of defining nonnegative forms is strictly positive on its remaining nonzero cone. Its level-one section is compact: an unbounded sequence normalized to length one would contradict strict positivity. Moving a nonvertex in both directions annihilating its active forms reaches new active constraints; induction decomposes into finitely many full-rank active solutions. Rational data give rational solutions. Homogenizing a polyhedron gives conv of finitely many rational generating POINTS plus cone of its exact rational recession directions. These points need not be vertices with lineality. Conversely coefficient elimination, pairing lower and upper bounds, produces finitely many weak inequalities, so the sum is a closed polyhedron. Cone separation follows by nearest projection: if a is outside a closed cone and z is closest, w=z−a has w·c≥0 for all cone c and w·a=−||w||²<0.

For a finite union of polyhedra, its CLOSED convex hull is conv(all point generators)+cone(all recession generators). The latter is closed because its hull is compact and its cone closed. The nontrivial reverse inclusion uses an explicit small-mass limit: with u in the closed hull and ray r based at a source point a, (1−delta)u+delta(a+r/delta) tends to u+r. Iterate over all finite rays. No unproved closure of an unbounded union hull is assumed.

For a full-domain epigraph with finite lower fibers, closedness attains the fibers. Finite convex functions are locally Lipschitz: upper bounds at cube vertices and reflection supply two-sided bounds, and extended secants bound differences on a smaller ball. Project a point just below a graph point to the closed epigraph and take a subsequential limit of the unit supporting normals. Its vertical component is positive: upward stability gives nonnegative component, while a zero component would impose a nontrivial lower bound on the entire spatial projection. Thus every point has an affine lower support. A finite epigraph inequality description divides by positive vertical components to express the lower function as a finite real affine maximum; its recession h is the maximum of their linear parts.

Rational walls with real heights follow from primal graph faces, not from arbitrary affine comparisons. For E=conv{(q,c)}+cone{(r,d),(0,1)} with rational q,r and real c,d, a lower support selects equality points and zero-slack rays; the vertical ray is excluded. Its projected lower face is a rational point hull plus rational cone. Lower graph projection is injective. Intersections are common faces because graph heights at the same spatial point coincide, and restricting the other support exposes the intersection. Faces of lower faces remain lower by a sufficiently small perturbation of their exposing functional; finite generator slacks preserve the strictly positive vertical component. The finitely many projected faces cover the domain and form a rational complex. Matching real affine coefficients solve a rational linear system evaluated on rational affine face bases. A rational kernel basis, with denominators cleared simultaneously on all cells, gives literal integral-slope/rational-constant PA functions. Their finite real span is exactly the matching real space. Thus REAL-PA membership is proved even for irrational actual heights.

Exact face distance. Let sigma be a rational closed full-dimensional cell in V and tau a nonempty face, H=aff(tau). Translate a rational tau point and use a RATIONAL split V=W⊕S, H=W, block l1 norms. An exposing form gives sigma∩H=tau. Write sigma={A_t t+A_s s≤b}; restricted violations of A_t t≤b are ≤J||s||. For a nearest point z of t in this restricted face polyhedron, w=t−z belongs to the cone of active outward normals: otherwise cone separation gives a direction with nonpositive active inequalities and w·v>0, feasible for short length by inactive slack and contradicting nearest-point variation. Use an independent active normal representation w=sum lambda_j n_j with sum lambda≤C||w||. Then ||w||²=sum lambda_j(n_j·t−b_j)≤C||w|| Delta(t). Cancellation and fixed norm equivalence yield ||t−z||_1≤K||s||_1. The relative face has full dimension in H. If H is a point, K=0; if tau=H, z=t and K=0. No irrational orthogonal projection is claimed rational.

Assume f is finite continuous convex and GLOBAL L-Lipschitz on sigma in these coordinates. Choose rational M,B>L with B≥L(K+1)+MK, N(t,s)=M||t||+B||s||, and F(x)=inf_{y∈sigma}[f(y)+N(x−y)]. A fixed y0 and the Lipschitz inequality give a finite lower bound f(y0)−L||x−y0||; evaluation at y0 gives a finite upper bound. Epsilon-minimizers and convexity prove F convex. Norm triangle inequalities give |F(x)−F(x')|≤N(x−x'). For x∈sigma all candidates are ≥f(x), and y=x gives exact equality. Strict M,B>L also bound minimizing y and give attainment, though the trace proof only needs infima.

For x=(h,0) and y=(t,s), choose z∈tau as above. Then f(y)≥f_tau(z)−L(K+1)||s|| and M||h−t||≥M||h−z||−MK||s||. The B inequality makes every candidate ≥f_tau(z)+M||h−z||. Conversely y=(z,0) is permitted. Hence on ALL H, F=g_M=inf_tau[f_tau+Mnorm], finite convex Lipschitz and exact on all tau. A finite family uses common M and individually large B_i. If uniformly bounded ambient p_y support all originals at EVERY y∈actual tau, choose N_i≥p_y on page directions. Each candidate is ≥f_i(y)+p_y(x−y), so the SAME p_y supports every entire F_i page at those actual y. This proves no support at H\tau.

For an actual REAL affine ell=a+b with a(r)>0 on EVERY nonzero rec(sigma) and |f−ell|≤C, enlarge norms also to dominate ell's global slopes and its analogous B inequality. Gamma=inf_sigma[ell+N] is exact on all sigma and has the analogous entire trace; two-sided candidate comparison gives |F−Gamma|≤C everywhere. From sigma=conv{q}+cone{r}, choose c>0 below all a(r)/||r|| for nonzero listed rays and finite D with ell(q)≥c||q||−D. Positivity excludes nonzero original lineality. Norm triangles give ell(y)≥c||y||−D and Gamma(x)≥min(c,M,B)||x||−D. Thus Gamma is proper, attains fibers, and has positive recession on every full-page nonzero ray. Its exact source epigraph has points (q,ell(q)), rays (r,a(r)), and vertical ray. Adding norm basis rays gives epi Gamma. The graph-face argument proves genuine finite rational-spatial REAL-PA, not an irrational-wall maximum. Original recession is unchanged by whole-cell equality. Agreement of original affine data on tau implies agreement on H, giving common whole reference traces for common M, but separate convexity is insufficient for PC gluing.

The diagnostic uses ambient e0=(1,0,0), v1=(0,1,0), v2=(0,0,1), v3=(0,−1,−1), sum v_i=0. Each complete page is span(e0,v_i), with proper original sigma_i={(t,s):s≥0,0≤t+s≤1}, shared tau=[0,1]e0, and f_i=ell_i=s. Original rec is generated by (−1,1) with slope1, global L=1, and p0=0 on tau. K=1,M=2,B=4 satisfy the exact trace inequality. The independent extensions are F_i(t,s)=inf_{0≤u≤1,r≥0}[r+2|t−u+r|+4|s−r|]. Their whole H trace is 2dist(t,[0,1]). Every candidate is ≥−2t+2u−r+4|s−r|≥−2t−s. Equality holds precisely when u=0,r=s≥0,t+s≤0. Thus R_i={s≥0,t+s≤0} is the projected lower face and its negative H ray is a face. At rational center −e0 the rational endpoints −e0+v_i/4 lie in these actual incident faces and have mean center. Their cost is 7/4−2=−1/4. This is a LEGAL PCC on compatible rational face carriers. Therefore equal entire traces and retained actual-face p0 do not suffice for outside compatibility. These proper original cells have unbalanced outer facets, so this is not an original balanced counterexample or a failure of regularization of the original target.

For completeness the separate full-affine majorant step is independently proved. If Gamma is finite convex rational-spatial REAL-PA on a complete affine V and f continuous convex is boundedly relative to it, write Gamma=max(a_j·x+b_j), h=max a_j·x and Delta=conv{a_j}; f−h is bounded. The conjugate f* is finite bounded exactly on Delta (separation gives infinity outside). It is convex lower semicontinuous and continuous even at polytope boundary: vertex values bound it above by B; inactive slacks at p provide a fixed feasible ray radius r in every direction q−p with q∈Delta. Convexity gives f*(q)≤f*(p)+(B−f*(p))||q−p||/r, and lower semicontinuity gives the converse limit. Rational primal samples approximate the supremum defining f* by continuity of f. Compactness therefore chooses finitely many rational samples, including any prescribed finite rational S, with f*−eta≤max_x[p·x−f(x)]≤f* on ALL Delta.

The epigraph of h has rational spatial generators: recession cones of Gamma's rational carrier cover V (along a fixed ray, one of finitely many closed cells contains an unbounded subsequence), and h is linear on each. Set E=conv{(x,f(x)):sample x}+epi h. Every affine support slope of f lies in Delta, since otherwise its excess over h along a ray contradicts bounded difference. Supremizing supports gives f(x+v)≤f(x)+h(v), so E⊂epi f. E is full-domain closed with attained fibers and rational-spatial REAL-PA lower P. Direct conjugation gives P*=max_samples(p·x−f(x)) on Delta and infinity outside. Double conjugation follows from full-space affine supports. Thus f≤P≤f+eta, and the sample lifts give equality on S. Compact hull plus closed cone has exactly that cone as its recession (divide a forward sequence by its parameter), so P has exact recession h. With eta_n=2^(−n), Q_n=P_n+4eta_n satisfies 4eta_n≤Q_n−f≤5eta_n and Q_{n+1}−f≤(5/2)eta_n, hence decreases uniformly. The shifted Q_n need not interpolate S. This applies separately to the constructed whole-page F_i,Gamma_i. It supplies no simultaneous face-trace or common-support approximation.

Artifacts and reruns: P05.1-paper.tex (complete proofs), argument.md (entire source-derived body), scope-and-gaps.md, source-application-ledger.md; python3 make_argument.py; python3 exact_checks.py > exact-checks.log 2>&1. The fresh Fraction program passed 1,577 assertions over its finite listed inputs, enumerating 35 active four-row LP subsets at each diagnostic point, and returned −1/4. Finite checks are exhaustive only for these lists, not proofs of the continuum claims above. Working299 is unreviewed and supplies no Lipschitz premise. General original all-face-PC regularization is still OPEN.

notes.summary: Independent proof of 301: actual REAL affine references with common star supports and positive original recession extend exactly to a compatible proper rational-spatial REAL-PA reference on arbitrary dependent complete rational pages sharing one H. Finite primal epigraphs, not max(G,ell), give rational walls and common ambient supports at EVERY H point.
notes.detailedSummary: For finite distinct equal-d pages with pairwise intersection exactly H, original full-dimensional cells have common actual tau with aff(tau)=H and sigma∩H=tau; actual affine ell agree on H and have positive slope on every nonzero original recession direction. Printed-PC rational endpoint tests with real zero-list weights yield a closed cost cone excluding (0,−1), and separation with strictly positive vertical coefficient yields p0 supporting all entire original cells. An ambient finite-generator hull plus rational norm cone gives proper G≤ell on originals, exact on tau. Its entire trace g dominates ell_tau, with all unbounded trace generators included. Page epigraph hulls plus norms lie above BOTH G and ell, preserving exact whole originals and whole g. Ambient G supports yield common supports at every h. A rational wall arrangement gives one genuine REAL-PA carrier; specified positive real page weights balance separately via saturated opposite normals. No normal independence, balancing for the initial form lemma, or MA premise is used. Nonlinear targets and multiple different overlaps are excluded.
notes.text:
This note independently proves all six working301 units. It uses the finite-cone, polyhedral-generation, closure, support, rational graph-face, and scalar-matching results proved in n1, declared as support. No supplied grant's mathematical theorem is used as an unproved premise.

Let finite DISTINCT complete rational affine d-pages V_i, d≥1, have EVERY pairwise intersection one rational H of dimension <d. The original rational closed full-dimensional cells sigma_i share the SAME nonempty face tau, aff(tau)=H and sigma_i∩H=tau. Actual REAL affine ell_i agree on H and ell_i,lin(r)>0 for EVERY nonzero original recession direction. Work in their rational ambient affine span E. A common form p0 supporting all ell_i on all original cells at one rational y∈ri(tau) is sufficient; if the glued affine star is printed PC, it follows as follows.

Translate y to zero. Each tangent cone Q_i is defined by inequalities active on tau; inactive slack ensures short assigned directions stay in the original cell. Choose finite rational Q_i generators w_j with assignments, including ± a rational H basis. Their ACTUAL REAL costs c_j=ell_i,lin(w_j) agree for shared H directions. For every real lambda_j≥0 with sum lambda_j w_j=0, choose one sufficiently small positive rational delta. The rational endpoints y+delta w_j are incident to tau, and real weights lambda_j/sum lambda are a legal printed PCC centered at y. Its inequality gives sum lambda c≥0. Consequently the finite cone C=cone{(w_j,c_j),(0,1)} excludes (0,−1). n1 proves it closed even with real heights and H lineality. Cone separation supplies q(w)+bt≥0 on C and negative at (0,−1), forcing b STRICTLY positive. Then p0=−q/b satisfies p0(w_j)≤c_j. Opposite H generators force p0|H=ell_tau,lin. Nonnegative generation supports all tangent cones, hence every entire sigma_i by affinity; H equality moves this same support to EVERY actual tau point. No balancing or quotient-direction independence is needed for this lemma. In a zero-dimensional span the vertical cone yields p0=0.

Take exact rational spatial point lists q_ia and recession lists r_ib for each ORIGINAL affine epigraph, with heights ell_i(q_ia) and slopes ell_i,lin(r_ib), plus vertical ray. Choose rational ambient coordinates and rational m>0 dominating p0 by m||v||_1. Form
E_G=conv{(q_ia,ell_i(q_ia))}+cone{(r_ib,ell_i,lin(r_ib)),(±e_j,m),(0,1)}.
By n1's far-ray small-mass argument this equals the CLOSED source-union hull plus epi(m||·||). It is closed, upward and has full spatial projection. Every generator lies above the common affine P(x)=ell_tau(y)+p0(x−y). Thus fibers are bounded below; one point plus norm rays gives a finite upper candidate on every x. Closedness attains the lower fiber G(x).

Choose c>0 below m and every positive ratio ell_i,lin(r)/||r|| for nonzero listed original rays. For all finite original points choose D with their heights≥c||q||−D. Any convex point plus conic ray representation then has height≥c||x||−D by norm triangle inequalities. Therefore G is proper with that uniform lower bound. Norm recession implies |G(x)−G(x')|≤m||x−x'||. Source inclusion gives G≤ell_i on all sigma_i; P gives exact G=ell_tau on ALL actual tau and the common p0 support there. The projected lower-face argument of n1 proves genuine finite rational-spatial REAL-PA despite irrational heights. The original spatial generating points were not presumed vertices in the presence of lineality.

Set g=G|H. It is finite convex Lipschitz proper, exact ell_tau on actual tau, and g≥ell_tau on ENTIRE H because P|H=ell_tau. Intersect G's rational lower-face carrier with H. Generate EVERY nonempty trace cell by rational h_a and recession w_b, including all unbounded cells and both signs of lineality where present. Lift points by actual g values and rays by h_G(w_b), the recession of G. Along each trace recession ray G is affine on that cell, so its slope equals h_G(w_b). Then
epi g=conv{(h_a,g(h_a))}+cone{(w_b,h_G(w_b)),(0,1)}.
One inclusion follows from convexity and recession stability; the other follows from each cell's exact point/ray representation and affine graph height. If H is a point, the list is one graph point plus vertical ray. Trace cell intersections remain common faces, and coefficient matching remains a rational linear system. All finite trace generators and recession rays are therefore accounted for.

For each page choose a rational polyhedral coordinate norm N_i dominating BOTH ell_i,lin(v) and h_G(v) on EVERY page direction. A sufficiently large rational multiple of the page l1 norm does this: bound the actual finite affine slopes and compose G's ambient Lipschitz estimate with the rational page inclusion. Define
E_i=closedconv(epi(ell_i+I_sigma_i) union epi g)+epi N_i.
By n1 this is EXACTLY the hull of original/trace lifted generating points plus the cone of original/trace recession rays, rational norm basis rays, and vertical ray. Hence it is closed with rational spatial generators and real heights.

ALL sources and rays are above BOTH G|V_i and ell_i. For G, original points satisfy G≤ell; trace points have equality; original rays belong to rec(E_G); trace rays have height h_G; norm rays dominate h_G. The closed convex epigraph of G is stable under each. For ell, original points/rays have equality, trace points satisfy g≥ell_tau, and dividing the latter inequality along each trace ray gives its slope≥ell_i,lin. Norm rays also dominate ell_i,lin. Thus E_i⊂epi G∩epi ell_i. A source point plus the norm cone makes every lower fiber finite; G bounds it below and closedness attains it. Its lower Gamma_i satisfies Gamma_i≥G and Gamma_i≥ell_i. Original epigraph inclusion gives Gamma_i≤ell_i on ALL sigma_i, so exact equality there. Trace epigraph inclusion gives Gamma_i|H≤g and Gamma_i≥G gives exact equality on ALL H. Gamma_i is convex proper, globally Lipschitz by norm recession, and rational-spatial REAL-PA by n1. Replacing this primal construction by max(G,ell_i) without a rational-wall proof is not justified and is not done.

At EVERY h∈H, a full ambient affine lower support p_h of G exists by n1. Gamma_i≥G and Gamma_i(h)=G(h) imply this SAME p_h supports all Gamma_i on ENTIRE pages. Off H only one of finitely many closed pages meets a sufficiently small neighborhood, giving ordinary convex page supports extendable to E. For any contained segment local affine supports imply convexity: subtract its endpoint chord; a positive interior maximum has zero supporting directional slope, making its maximum set open and closed in the connected open interval, contradicting the zero endpoint limit. For any legal PCC, the segment from its center to each endpoint lies in an incident convex cell; its initial ambient support and convex secants give Gamma(x_j)≥Gamma(x)+p(x_j−x). Summation proves the PCC with arbitrary real weights. Thus the gluing is continuous printed PC on the complete book.

For one genuine common rational carrier, extend every rational page-wall and H equation to E using rational linear algebra; take the finite ambient hyperplane arrangement and restrict it to all pages. Its subdivisions agree on H and refine each projected graph carrier. No unrelated real coefficients introduce new comparison walls. Matching real affine data then lie in the finite real span of literal PA by n1. The lower bound Gamma_i≥G≥c||x||−D yields positive recession slope on every nonzero ray of every new cell. Assign any specified actual positive real constant page weights. At each page-subdivision facet the saturated primitive inward quotient classes on its two sides are opposite and the page weight equal, so contributions cancel separately on EVERY page, including H facets when codimension one. Summing pages proves balancing without independence. Rational weights are the literal BMPS convention; real weights here refer to the explicitly proved real balancing equation, with no MA conclusion.

Point trace H=0 is included above. A zero-dimensional complete space is a point with constant extension and vacuous recession/balancing. A lone page with tau=sigma uses the proper auxiliary extension from n1; no inter-page condition arises. Distinct pages cannot have a nonempty intersection of their full dimension.

The specific dependent diagnostic of n1 has an additional explicit compatible reference: ambient R(t,a,b)=max(|a|,|b|,−t,t−1). On each original cell a,b are s times its page vector, so max(|a|,|b|)=s; −t=s−u≤s and t−1=u−s−1≤s. Hence R=s on the WHOLE original cell. Its whole trace is dist(t,[0,1]); R≥(|t|+|a|+|b|)/3−1, so it is proper, ambient convex rational PA and printed PC. This verifies repair of the PARTICULAR incompatible independent extension while leaving its −1/4 failure intact. This explicit R is an additional example, not a numerically inferred output of unspecified norm choices in the general construction.

Artifacts: P05.1-paper.tex, argument.md, source-application-ledger.md, scope-and-gaps.md, exact_checks.py, certificate-input.json, exact-output.json. Reruns: python3 exact_checks.py > exact-checks.log 2>&1; python3 make_argument.py; python3 build.py > build-rerun-driver.log 2>&1. The exact code checked the explicit reference on its finite listed original points and its lower bound there, not the arbitrary-reference theorem. The theorem is the proof above. This is an admitted affine-reference extension, not an extension theorem for nonlinear targets, several different overlaps, or extra nonincident pages; no original classification is closed.

notes.summary: Independent proofs of 302–303: for the three dependent complete pages and rational A≥1, the GLOBAL restriction distance from f_A=max(0,s−Au) to ALL finite-valued continuous printed-PC competitors is exactly (A−1)/2, attained. Whole-page convexity and a legal SMALL rational PCC justify the far inequality; unbounded integers prove the floor. Exact extension fails for A>1. Partial support is unbalanced and already PA-PC, so original regularization remains OPEN.
notes.detailedSummary: The original cells s≥0,0≤u=t+s≤1 share actual tau=[0,1]e0, gamma=s, rec slope1, global cell Lipschitz A and common p0=0. For any finite-valued continuous printed-PC full-book F, inherited rational cell tests plus local breakpoint PCCs and continuity imply whole-page convexity, without coarsening or PA. Short rational endpoints y_T+delta T v_i incident to the actual minimal face give F(y_T)≤average F(z_i) after convex secants. With global error epsilon and every integer T≥max(1,A−1), z_i=(-T,T), r_1=(-T,T+1) have target T and T+1−A; the page secant yields F(y_T)≥AT−(2T+1)epsilon while the upper bound is T+epsilon. Thus epsilon≥(A−1)T/[2(T+1)], and the unbounded limit proves (A−1)/2. Ambient convex rational-PA max(0,−t)−(A−1)/2 attains it globally. The exact A=2 contradiction is 2≤F(−e0)≤1. No full-reference growth or PA restriction is imposed on competitors and no arbitrary-full-reference boundedness is claimed for the witness.
notes.text:
This note gives self-contained proofs of working302 and working303. It uses no granted approximation, MA, or earlier local mathematical result.

In rational ambient R³ let e0=(1,0,0), v1=(0,1,0), v2=(0,0,1), v3=(0,−1,−1); v1+v2+v3=0. Complete pages V_i=span(e0,v_i) intersect pairwise in H=R e0, since every two transverse vectors are independent. On each page take the original full-dimensional closed rational cell sigma_i={(t,s):s≥0,0≤u=t+s≤1}. Their common actual face is tau=[0,1]e0, with aff(tau)=H and sigma_i∩H=tau. Each recession cone is the nonnegative ray (−1,1). Actual affine gamma=s has slope1 on this ray.

For rational A≥1 define f_A,i=max(0,−At+(1−A)s)=max(0,s−Au). It is finite continuous rational-affine PA on a genuine rational subdivision. Its gradients are zero and (−A,1−A), so the coordinate l1 Lipschitz bound is A; affine rational data with matching faces yield genuine rational-spatial REAL-PA by clearing denominators. On original cells f_A−gamma=max(−s,−Au) lies in [−A,0]. The tau trace is zero and f_A≥0 everywhere, so p0=0 supports all entire original cells at every tau point. The partial gluing is printed PC: a convex cell contained in a finite union of affine pages lies in one page, since otherwise its relative interior would be covered by finitely many proper affine subspaces, whose nonzero vanishing affine equations have a nonzero product that cannot vanish on an open set. Any legal center outside H uses cells in its sole page and ordinary convexity; at tau the global zero supports give Jensen for all endpoint assignments and real weights. Original recession of f_A is1: along (−1,1), u stays fixed and for large s the active expression is s−Au. Thus the target itself is already proper partial rational-PA PC, boundedly relative to gamma, with an available constant regularization sequence. The outer original facets u=0 and u=1 have an uncancelled positive-page normal, so this PARTIAL support is unbalanced. No original positive-balanced regularization counterexample is asserted.

We prove whole-page convexity for EVERY finite-valued continuous printed-PC F on the COMPLETE book, with no PA, reference, properness, or growth assumption. A finite or locally finite rational carrier suffices; locally finite carriers meet any compact segment in finitely many cells. Within each inherited convex cell, rational endpoint tests are legal because the center's minimal face is a face of that cell. Rational points are dense in rational polyhedra (use rational kernel bases and preserve inactive strict inequalities). Continuity therefore extends these convex inequalities to real endpoints and weights. For a rational-endpoint page segment, rational inequalities give finitely many rational breakpoints. At each breakpoint q, choose sufficiently short rational left/right endpoints a,b in the adjacent actual cells. Both closed cells contain q and its minimal face, so the PCC centered at q is LEGAL. It gives [F(q)−F(a)]/(q−a)≤[F(b)−F(q)]/(b−q). Continuity extends near-endpoint inequalities to real a,b. On the adjacent intervals convexity orders secants. Their limiting left/right derivatives are finite: the left is bounded above by a fixed right secant and below by an interior left secant, and conversely for the right. The left derivative is at most the right. Secants crossing q are length-weighted averages of these ordered secants; hence the ordered-secant criterion holds across the breakpoint. Induction through the finite partition proves convexity on the whole rational segment. Approximate arbitrary real page endpoints by rational ones and use continuity. This proof uses inherited cells and actual local breakpoint PCCs, without illegal coarsening.

For rational T>0 set y_T=−T e0 and z_i=y_T+T v_i. The far z_i may be NONincident to the actual minimal face at y_T. Instead, along each rational page ray, finite local carrier intervals give a common sufficiently small rational delta∈(0,1) with endpoints w_i=y_T+delta T v_i in actual cells containing y_T. Such cells contain its minimal face by the common-face axiom. Their mean is y_T, so the SHORT PCC with weights1/3 is legal. Whole-page convexity gives F(w_i)≤(1−delta)F(y_T)+delta F(z_i). Summation and the small PCC cancel the (1−delta) term and prove F(y_T)≤(F(z_1)+F(z_2)+F(z_3))/3. We have derived the far inequality rather than treating it as a legal far PCC.

Exact extension obstruction. If F agrees with f_A on all original cells and A>1, at T=1 the z_i have f_A(z_i)=1, so F(−e0)≤1. Choose rational 0<u*<min(1,1/(A−1)) and q=(-1,1+u*) in page1. It is in the original cell interior and the affine expression L=−At+(1−A)s is strictly positive there. Thus F=L on an OPEN page neighborhood of q. For a convex whole-page F, this affine expression supports globally: on the line from q toward any x, the initial affine slope is at most every later secant. Consequently F(−e0)≥L(-1,0)=A>1, contradiction. At A=2 choose q=(-1,3/2), giving exactly 2≤F(−e0)≤1. This argument imposes no target-exterior growth, reference, or PA condition on F.

Sharp distance. Define epsilon(F)=sup_{union sigma_i}|F−f_A|, allowing infinity, and D_A its infimum over ALL finite-valued continuous printed-PC functions on the complete book.
